purpose: Translate Q066 descriptive findings into two explicit, mechanistically distinct follow-up hypotheses without performance evaluation, tuning, family ranking or holdout selection.

mechanisms.question: Can a fixed exposure transformation based on cross-alpha sleeve return dependence reduce adverse-period common-mode risk while retaining meaningful alpha exposure?
mechanisms.information_input: Trailing realized return correlation among the fixed alpha sleeves available in the fresh validation study.
mechanisms.intervention: Scale aggregate alpha exposure downward during sufficiently high cross-alpha common-mode dependence; recovery is rule-based and lagged.
mechanisms.distinction_from_q030_risk_c: Risk-C measured dependence among underlying cross-sectional asset returns; E1 measures dependence among alpha-sleeve return streams.

mechanisms.question: Can a fixed rebalance deadband suppress economically material turnover/cost drag from high-churn mechanisms without materially changing their signal identity?
mechanisms.information_input: Only the already generated fixed target weights and prior held weights; no new predictive information.
mechanisms.intervention: Apply a fixed, ex-ante minimum-change rule before executing a target-weight update, with deterministic carry-forward behavior.
mechanisms.distinction_from_signal_tuning: E2 changes implementation churn rather than the alpha signal definition.

required_sequence: freeze exact parameters and timing for each mechanism ex ante
point-in-time validation of the frozen implementation
only then a fixed-rule performance trial under the unchanged 13-gate contract
